text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Mubarak will explain to the World Economic Forum at Davos the results of Egypt's economic restructuring and the Middle East peace process. The president will meet Palestinian leader Arafat and hold talks with Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu today about the stage following redeployment.
- World Bank head says Egypt and the bank have identical views in all fields.
- Supreme Constitutional Court throws out lawsuits which alleged that privatisation of state companies was unconstitutional.
- Deputy head of International Monetary Fund says Egypt's economic restructuring programme is 100 percent successful.

- Mubarak today speaks at the international economic forum in Davos. He will reaffirm the necessity of advanced countries helping out developing economies. President holds intensive contacts with world leaders and businessmen.
- By Israeli orders...prayer is not allowed in the Al-Aqsa mosque in Jerusalem. U.N. secretary-general admits that the organisation cannot do anything to Israel.
- Stock market to close for four days from February 7 for Eid al-Fitr holidays.
- Mubarak tells the world about the success of Egypt's economic experiments. Investment poured into Egypt along with the growth of stability and development.
- Egypt to release 2,300 repentant prisoners on the occasion of Eid al-Fitr.
